title: Orizon Agents: evidence index for the Stellar Instaward

sow.note: This index follows the approved SOW v4, dated 2026-08-01. Section 6.1 says what evidence each deliverable owes, section 6.2 is the checklist the Ambassador Chapter Lead marks (Present, Partial or Missing), and section 6.3 lists the eleven success metrics. One of them, metric m03, was removed from the sprint's requirements on 2026-09-30, so the metrics table shows the other ten and the removal is stated under Disclosures. Each deliverable below repeats the SOW's Evidence Type and Description word for word. Every piece of evidence has a status and a link you can open, and anything missing or partly done says why in plain words.

snapshot.method: Every on-chain link was re-read on 2026-09-30, after escrow v2 was deployed and the live API switched to it that day, from Stellar's public testnet record (Horizon, horizon-testnet.stellar.org). Each transaction was confirmed successful, and the date beside it is the day the ledger recorded it, in UTC. Contract activity was cross-checked on Stellar Expert. The 21 transactions of the team's test runs, including the first dispute's refund and dispute rating, were also re-verified successful by the backend's evidence tool (demo_evidence), and the screenshots and recordings of 2026-09-30 were taken from the live site with no wallet connected. Every web link was opened without logging in and returned a working page. A wallet counts as the team's when it is in the team wallet register (backend repository, app/data/team_wallets.json), is declared for it in an open pull request that this index names, or holds a platform role on the contracts. The metrics were re-measured the same day, at 10:42 UTC, by the backend's read-only generator (scripts/sow_metrics). Metrics 5 and 8 were measured again at 15:30 UTC, after the first dispute was refunded, and metrics 1 and 2 at 15:48 UTC, after five more outside wallets registered agents; their rows are from those runs, and the other rows are as measured at 10:42. Metric m03 was removed from the sprint's requirements on 2026-09-30, so its row from the generator was left out and the other ten are shown. The platform lists outside operators publicly, with their wallets and agent ids, so this index links each outside registration and wallet. Those links were added on 2026-10-01 from a fresh read-only run of the same generator, and the live adoption counter was re-read that day to confirm them: 11 outside agents from 7 wallets, one bound to an endpoint and none settled. Nothing was signed, paid or submitted to make this snapshot.

items.claim: At least 3 settlement transactions on Stellar Expert, each with its on-chain receipt and attestation.
items.note: Present: 3 of 3. On 2026-09-30 three workflows settled on the live escrow v2 (CCNO5…5VC4), each with its settlement and its attestation seal on Stellar Expert. All three are the team's own test runs, not outside operators' work. The buyers were team keys: GB4K6…YKAYKK paid for run 1 and GCNQA…A2GP for runs 2 and 3. Both agents, calculatorai and keyboardai, are owned by the team's admin wallet GA7AI…5OQV, which received each payout. The settlements and seals were signed by the platform's production key GDB4N…CDHP. Run 1 paid 0.01 XLM to calculatorai, run 2 paid 0.2 XLM to keyboardai and run 3 paid 0.01 XLM to calculatorai, and the test harness's settlement checks passed for each. The buyer key GCNQA…A2GP was created for these runs on 2026-09-30; backend pull request #96 added it to the team wallet register the same day. No outside operator's agent was paid. Before escrow v2 no payment settled during the sprint: the v1 escrow could not move a buyer's funds to a different wallet (defect D-039, contracts issue #3), so none of its authorizations since 2026-09-07 was charged. Its 8 older 'charged' events are pre-sprint self-payments and do not count (see the notes).

disclosures.title: Testnet only
disclosures.text: SOW §3.6: "Testnet: all Instaward work is built and validated on Stellar testnet for this sprint — no mainnet funds are at risk. Orizon's contracts are also deployed on Stellar mainnet outside this award; none of that deployment is funded by, or in scope for, this Instaward." Every Stellar Expert link in this index points at the testnet explorer. Testnet money has no real value.

disclosures.title: Anyone can register; payment is still run by the platform
disclosures.text: SOW §3.8: "Deliverable 1 makes registration permissionless; it does not make settlement permissionless." Any wallet can register an agent without asking Orizon. Paying agents, writing ratings and deciding disputes are still done by keys the platform holds. The contract's register call was already open to any wallet: story 1.01 audited it and needed no contract change, so Deliverable 1 has no contracts pull request.

disclosures.title: Payments are released by a single platform key
disclosures.text: SOW §3.8: "the settler is not permissionless. The settler (the role that executes charge and will operate this sprint's dispute/partial-credit path) is a single platform-held backend key, fixed at contract deployment; the contract exposes no settler-rotation function." This is still true of the live escrow, v2 since 2026-09-30: one team-held key releases payments, with no multi-signature or threshold control.
disclosures.changed_since_sow: Two changes. First, the SOW says one keypair also holds the admin, scorer and sealer roles. On 2026-09-19 the rating (scorer) and sealing (sealer) roles moved from the admin wallet GA7AI…5OQV to a separate production key, GDB4N…CDHP; the two transactions are linked under Repositories & Deployments. The admin wallet still holds the admin role and was the settler on the v1 escrow. On escrow v2, live since 2026-09-30, the production key GDB4N…CDHP signs the settlements, and it also pays the dispute credit. Both keys are held by the team. Second, escrow v2 adds a set_settler function, so the settler can be replaced. v2 was merged (contracts pull request #4, 2026-09-28) and deployed to testnet on 2026-09-30 (contracts pull request #6), so the live escrow can now rotate its settler; it has not been rotated.

disclosures.title: How payment works, and why no payment settled before escrow v2
disclosures.text: SOW §3.8: "the settler executes charge, which moves USDC directly from the buyer to the agent owner's wallet through the Stellar Asset Contract, the platform never takes custody of funds." On the v1 escrow, the live escrow until 2026-09-30, this did not work: charge could not move funds from a buyer who was not also the settler (defect D-039, contracts issue #3). No payment between two different wallets ever settled on it.
disclosures.changed_since_sow: Escrow v2 fixes this by holding the buyer's authorized amount from the moment the buyer authorizes, then paying each operator at settlement and returning the rest to the buyer. That means the platform's contract does hold funds for a while, which changes the SOW's "never takes custody" statement. v2 was merged in the contracts repository (pull request #4, 2026-09-28) and deployed to testnet on 2026-09-30 as CCNO5…5VC4 (recorded in contracts pull request #6). The live backend settles through it (pull request #88), and its readiness report shows escrow version 2. The first three settlements through it are team test runs (see Deliverable 4).

disclosures.title: Refunds are credits paid from the platform's own funds
disclosures.text: When a dispute is upheld, the platform sends the buyer a credit from its own balance. It is not taken back from the agent's owner, and it is not drawn from the buyer's authorization. The platform's signing key (GDB4N…CDHP) pays dispute credits, writes ratings and seals attestations, and it signs the settlements on escrow v2, live since 2026-09-30. The v1 escrow's settler was the admin key (GA7AI…5OQV). The credit is the price of the disputed step, capped by what the payment actually moved. A credit above the per-refund ceiling (MAX_REFUND_USDC) is refused outright, not reduced to the ceiling, and nothing is paid. Refunds were switched on with escrow v2 (the live readiness report shows them on). The first credit was paid on 2026-09-30: 0.01 XLM from GDB4N…CDHP to the team buyer key GCNQA…A2GP, the full charge of a disputed step on a team test run, since the live credit policy (dispute_credited_fraction) is 1.0 (transaction cb2c5792…1e25f; see Deliverable 3).
disclosures.changed_since_sow: The SOW says the refund is executed by the settler "within the buyer's envelope" (§3.8) and "against the buyer's authorization envelope" (§4.1). The v1 escrow had no refund function and never held funds, so there was nothing inside the envelope to return. The refund became a separate transfer funded by the platform (backend decision records ADR 0002 and ADR 0008).

disclosures.title: An agent's server address is stored off-chain
disclosures.text: The on-chain agent record holds its owner, id, name, skills and price. It has no field for the address of the operator's server. The operator links that address to their agent in Orizon's database, proving they own the agent by signing a message with the owner wallet (backend decision record ADR 0001). So where Orizon sends an agent's work is decided by Orizon's database, not by the chain.
disclosures.changed_since_sow: Not in the SOW. It was chosen in Week 1 (decision spike 1.06) instead of redeploying the registry, which would have changed the published contract addresses.

disclosures.title: Ratings and dispute decisions are made by the platform
disclosures.text: SOW §3.8: "reputation ratings can only be submitted by the platform's scorer key. Settlement, rating submission, and dispute resolution are therefore trusted, permissioned operations today." This is still true. Only the platform's production key writes ratings, and disputes are decided by the platform's operator: the first, on a team test run, was upheld on 2026-09-30.
disclosures.changed_since_sow: The SOW says a rating is recorded once per settled job. The platform now rates every paid run whether or not its payment settles, so that failed deliveries are also recorded (backend pull request #57). Of the 40 ratings written during the sprint, 36 come from runs whose payment did not settle, including the three failed runs of the team's deliberate faulty test agent, 3 from the team's settled escrow v2 test runs of 2026-09-30, and 1 is the dispute rating written when the first dispute was upheld that day.

disclosures.title: Small payments barely move a reputation score
disclosures.text: Every agent starts from a prior score of 7000 of 10000 (3.50 stars), which counts as much as 12 XLM of rated jobs, and each rating is weighted by what its job was paid (the live settings: /api/stellar/reputation/params). So ratings on 0.01 XLM jobs barely move a score: calculatorai's two ratings of 95 out of 100 on 2026-09-30 took it from 7000 to 7004, and the upheld dispute's rating later that day took it to 6999 (Deliverable 3). The ★ 3.50 on the Deliverable 2 plan card is that on-chain score, but it is numerically the same as the starting estimate; what differs on the card is the missing '≈' estimate mark. The stronger proof that reputation gates routing is the deliberate faulty test agent left out below the floor in Deliverable 2.

notes.title: How to read the links
notes.text: Stellar Expert (stellar.expert) is a free public website that shows everything recorded on the Stellar network. A transaction link opens one recorded action, with its date and a 'Successful' mark. A contract link opens a program on the network; its Events tab lists everything it has recorded. An account link opens a wallet and its history. Every such link here uses the testnet explorer. GitHub pull request links show 'Merged' or 'Open' at the top of the page. Nothing needs a login.

notes.title: USDC in the SOW, XLM on testnet
notes.text: The SOW describes payments in USDC. On testnet, Orizon's escrow is set up with Stellar's native asset, XLM, through its standard asset contract (CDLZF…GCYSC). So every payment and refund amount in this index is in testnet XLM. The code does not depend on the asset; metric 4 is measured on that basis.

notes.title: How an outside operator is told apart from the team
notes.text: The team keeps a public register of every wallet it controls, in the backend repository (app/data/team_wallets.json). An agent counts as outside only when its owner is not in that register and holds no platform role. 14 of the 25 registrations so far are by team wallets, and each is labelled that way here; the 14th, on 2026-09-30, is the deliberate faulty test agent faulty_test_v2 (see Deliverable 2). The other 11 are by 7 outside operators: 6 agents from 2 operators on 2026-09-29 and 5 agents from 5 more operators on 2026-09-30. One is bound to a parked web page and the other 10 are not bound to any endpoint (see Deliverable 4). The escrow v2 test runs of 2026-09-30 used team wallets only: the buyers GB4K6…YKAYKK, which is in the register, and GCNQA…A2GP, added to the register on 2026-09-30 (backend pull request #96); and the admin wallet GA7AI…5OQV, which owns the agents and authorized the faulty agent's runs.

notes.title: The 8 'charged' events on the escrow do not count
notes.text: The v1 PaymentEscrow's Events tab shows 8 'charged' events, and the AttestationRegistry shows 8 seals from the same days. All 16 are from 2026-05-13 to 2026-06-09, months before the sprint began on 2026-09-07. In each, the team's admin wallet was the buyer, the settler and the agent's owner, so it paid itself and no money changed hands. They are linked under metric 4 so you can check them, and they are not counted toward any target. The AttestationRegistry's 3 seals of 2026-09-30 are different: they seal the team's escrow v2 test runs (see Deliverable 4).

notes.title: Corrections to evidence submitted earlier
notes.text: 1. The Week-1 bundle presented transaction 9b8ffaa4…9a68 (2026-09-12, 0.054 XLM) as "a real refund landed on testnet", and a backend record called it the SOW §6.1 Deliverable 3 artifact. It was a test transfer from the admin wallet to a team key (GBI2I…ADBH), tied to no dispute and no payment. It shows only that the platform key can send a transfer. It is not Deliverable 3 evidence. 2. The Week-1 bundle marked Deliverable 1 as met using two registrations: dan_w1_probe, signed by the team's admin wallet, and sign_probe_bb5c12, signed by a team probe key. Both are team wallets, so neither is the externally owned registration Deliverable 1 asks for. 3. The Week-1 bundle said the refund record was on the backend's main branch. It was removed on 2026-09-22 (backend pull request #42), so that link no longer works. 4. The Week-2 technical document called the 40-second Week-2 build clip on X a demo video. It is a build update, not the 3–5 minute demo the SOW asks for.

notes.title: Test runs are not deliverable evidence
notes.text: QA proved the dispute path by running the real backend against a separate drill ReputationLedger (CAFZB…5CRP) and a test asset (CCW66…GUENL), signed by a QA drill key (GA45I…EGZ2), on 2026-09-25 and 2026-09-26. Those transactions are real, but they are a mechanism test on a separate drill ledger, not deliverable evidence, so none is linked here. Likewise, QA frame RF-17, which showed the reputation floor excluding an agent, used a plan written by the test; it is not linked, and the live exclusion of 2026-09-30 under Deliverable 2 takes its place.

notes.title: Targets come from SOW v4
notes.text: An earlier SOW, v3 (2026-06-11), set lower targets: at least 1 outside agent, 1 outside wallet and 2 settled workflows. The approved v4 (2026-08-01) raised them to 2, 2 and 3. This index measures against v4. Today they stand at 11, 7 and 0, which meets the first two v4 targets and misses the third. The first two count registrations only: no outside agent is bound to a working endpoint yet (see Deliverable 4).

notes.title: Repository addresses
notes.text: The SOW names the repositories under github.com/ALGOREX-PH. They moved to the Bl0cksmiths organisation, and the old addresses redirect to the new ones, so this index links the new addresses directly.

notes.title: The live API is updated by hand
notes.text: The live API on Render does not update itself when code merges; the team deploys it by hand. It was deployed on 2026-09-29 with everything merged to the backend's main branch up to pull request #94, including the adoption counter (backend pull request #89) and settlement through escrow v2 (backend pull request #88). Until 2026-09-30 that settlement could not run, because escrow v2 was not yet on testnet and the live escrow was v1. On 2026-09-30 escrow v2 was deployed and the live API's escrow setting (STELLAR_PAYMENT_ESCROW) was pointed at it; its readiness report now shows escrow version 2 and refunds switched on, with disputes stored in Postgres.

notes.title: orizons.xyz switches back to mainnet after the sprint
notes.text: For this sprint orizons.xyz was switched to Stellar testnet. After the sprint it is due to switch back to mainnet. This index is a snapshot of 2026-09-30; if the site shows mainnet when you open it, the testnet evidence here is still on the testnet explorer links.

notes.title: How long testnet keeps this evidence
notes.text: Stellar's testnet was last reset on 2025-12-17, and its public record keeps full history since then, so every link here still opens. The Stellar Development Foundation resets testnet from time to time. A reset would erase this history, and the links would stop working.
